title: THEORETICAL INVESTIGATION OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PLACE ATTACHMENT AND WELL-BEING
research_focus: To theoretically investigate the intricate relationship between place attachment and well-being, exploring the multifaceted dimensions of human experience and the significance of place, and to identify similarities and differences between these concepts through a theoretical framework and an exemplified focus group study.

sample_context.description: Six participants (three females, three males) aged 20-29, living in the 100. Yıl Neighborhood in Ankara, Turkey for at least 3 years. Participants were recruited through the social network of a local café owner and voluntarily agreed to participate.
sample_context.setting: 100. Yıl Workers Blocks Neighborhood, Çankaya district, Ankara, Turkey, a neighborhood with strong community relations and cultural preservation, near Middle East Technical University (METU) and Çankaya University.

findings.description: Opportunities for social activities, including cultural and artistic ones, contribute to individuals' attachment to a place by fostering productivity and self-improvement.
supporting_quotes: Being in contact with too many young people and my need to be productive lead me to engage in social activities. Social activity opportunities are quite important for me. The place where I live provides me with various cultural and social activities
Music is part of my identity. As a musician, I also see social activities as opportunities to improve myself artistically

findings.antecedent: Social relationships (family roots, loved ones, strong social relationships)
findings.description: Strong social relationships, including family and loved ones, foster a sense of safety and belonging, which in turn strengthens attachment to a place and evokes a duty of loyalty.
supporting_quotes: I feel safe here because I have family roots, loved ones, and strong social relationships in here. This can be considered a justification for attachment to a place
I have so many memories in here with the people I love. I feel attached here because I feel like I have a duty of loyalty here

findings.antecedent: Memories (knowledge, activities with loved ones, emotional experiences)
findings.description: Positive memories, especially those linked to activities with loved ones and emotional experiences, build knowledge and self-identity, contributing to a strong attachment to a place and a sense of duty of loyalty and settledness.
supporting_quotes: I think that having knowledge about a place is built on memories. The activities we enjoyed in with our loved ones and some emotional experiences are the things that connect us to the place we live in

findings.description: A deep sense of familiarity with a place, including its problems and one's self-identification within it, fosters a strong sense of connectedness and attachment.
supporting_quotes: There are so many things that describe me where I am attached, that I can see myself. I know the problems of this city and neighborhood; I know this place. That is why I am familiar with here in every sense. Being familiar with the place is one of the reasons that explains my connectedness to it

findings.antecedent: Being active and productive (earning money, hiking, nature)
findings.consequent: Well-being (feeling better, happier, financial security, clear thinking, awareness, recognition, self-impact, feeling good about self)
findings.description: Engaging in active and productive behaviors, such as earning money or spending time in nature, contributes to overall well-being by fostering positive emotions, financial security, cognitive clarity, and a sense of self-impact.
supporting_quotes: Firstly, being active and productive makes me feel better and happier if I earn something in return. It might be the first example that comes into mind but if I can be active and productive, I can earn money and it is important to feel secured financially

I enjoy hiking. Being in nature creates an environment that allows me to feel active and think clearly, making me more productive. Even after leaving nature, I return with a sense of awareness, and recognition. I can see the effects of this in my life. It serves as a means for me to make an impact for myself or others and all these processes enables me to feel good about myself

findings.antecedent: Sense of togetherness (being with people, sharing space/time, common solutions, helping others)
findings.description: The feeling of togetherness, whether with familiar people or strangers in a shared space, enhances productivity, happiness, and a sense of safety and well-being, particularly through collaborative problem-solving and mutual support.
supporting_quotes: Firstly, the sense of togetherness is undoubtedly significant both individually and socially. However, for me, it can be considered as the key to many things. The feeling of being together with either people I know well or strangers, sharing a common space and time, increases my productivity. Searching for common solutions with these people and helping others makes me feel good. At the same time, knowing that we are together and I am not alone makes me basically feel happy and safe

findings.antecedent: Enjoying life (pleasantness, aesthetics of a place, enjoyment from situations, pleasure)
findings.description: Enjoying life, experiencing pleasantness, appreciating the aesthetics of a place, and finding enjoyment in various situations directly contribute to feelings of happiness and overall well-being.
supporting_quotes: I think enjoying life in every aspect is directly related to happiness and feeling good. It may be difficult to express this but I will try to describe this pleasantness. What I mean by pleasure can sometimes be result of viewing the aesthetics of a place, and sometimes it can be described as a feeling of enjoyment that arises as a result of any situation. This feeling of pleasure triggers my happiness and I feel better in some way

findings.antecedent: Territoriality (sense of ownership, feeling at home, sense of togetherness)
findings.description: A strong sense of territoriality, including feeling at home and having ownership over a place, combined with a sense of togetherness with its inhabitants, enhances individuals' well-being and happiness.
supporting_quotes: When I think of this place where I am attached to, I feel like at home. I have a sense of ownership here. I experience the same thing when I establish a sense of togetherness with the people I am with here. It is impossible for me to feel this way when I am in a place where I feel like a guest or a stranger. Feeling like a homeowner makes me feel better and happier

findings.antecedent: Being understood by people, sense of togetherness, desire for challenge, prosocial behaviors
findings.description: Collective relations emerge as an outcome when individuals feel understood by others, experience a sense of togetherness, pursue challenges, and engage in prosocial behaviors within a place.
The ability to feel freedom is crucial for an individual's well-being, which is also linked to economic welfare and the fulfillment of needs.
supporting_quotes: I think freedom is very important for me. A person needs to feel freedom to feel good about themselves. Of course, this freedom is related to many things, but reaching a level of economic welfare is also very important. Because fulfilling many needs is somewhat dependent on financial situations.

findings.antecedent: Feeling safe (being understood, accepted, loved ones, family)
findings.consequent: Well-being (feeling good, psychological and mental health)
findings.description: A sense of safety, derived from feeling understood, accepted, and being surrounded by loved ones and family, is a prominent factor for well-being, as its absence negatively impacts psychological and mental health.
supporting_quotes: For me, feeling safe was the prominent concept, I think. When I think about both being understood, being accepted, and my loved ones, these concepts that provide me with this sense of security are the factors that make me feel good. The fact that my loved ones and family are here and that I feel understood and accepted also shows that this place provides me with these things. Because when I don't feel safe, I am really negatively affected psychologically and mentally. When I look at it in general, attachment to a place and well-being overlap a lot, I think. Because, for example, to feel attached to a place, I need to feel safe and free. When I feel this way, I feel good...

derived_hypotheses: Any form of attachment to a place might have impacts on well-being states of people.
The creation and maintenance of livable and meaningful places will nourish individuals’ attachments and consequently enhance their well-being.
mechanism_candidates: Environmental Design (creating spaces that meet functional needs, incorporate nature, provide green spaces, design for inclusivity, reflect local culture/history to foster attachment and well-being)
Place-Responsive Design (integrating local context, heritage, and identity into planning to foster belonging and attachment)
Adaptive Planning and Flexibility (designing frameworks that accommodate changing needs, technology, and social transformations for sustained attachment and well-being)
User-Centered Design (prioritizing individual experiences, psychological needs, preferences, and behaviors in planning to promote well-being, satisfaction, and ownership)
Sense of Place (designing places with distinct character to evoke identity, meaning, and attachment, positively impacting psychological well-being)
Biophilic Design (integrating nature and natural elements into the built environment to reduce stress, improve cognitive function, and enhance well-being)
Inclusive and Equitable Spaces (designing public spaces that cater to diverse psychological needs, promote social interaction, community engagement, and safety)

Promoting Social Interaction and Community (designing public spaces that encourage spontaneous encounters, community gathering, and support community-led initiatives to combat social isolation and improve well-being)
Mental Health Considerations (addressing noise pollution, air quality, natural light access, and creating stress-reducing spaces in planning to support mental health)
Immersion and Presence in Virtual Environments (realistic graphics, spatial audio, interactive elements to evoke 'being there' feeling, enhancing psychological impact)
Personalization and Agency in Virtual Environments (avatar customization, adjustable settings, user-controlled interactions to enhance psychological well-being and empowerment)
Social Interaction and Connection in Virtual Environments (voice/video chat, collaborative activities, shared virtual spaces to address psychological needs for social connection and combat isolation)

Emotional Engagement and Expression in Virtual Environments (immersive storytelling, compelling narratives, interactive elements to elicit emotional responses, supporting psychological well-being and self-reflection)
Privacy and Security in Virtual Environments (robust data protection, user consent, clear guidelines for appropriate behavior/content to ensure psychological safety and authentic engagement)
Balance with Real-World Engagement in Virtual Environments (designing virtual environments to complement and enhance, rather than replace, real-world experiences for balanced psychological health)
Safety and Basic Needs (providing shelter, clean water, food, medical aid in disaster recovery to ensure physical well-being and psychological recovery)
Place Attachment and Sense of Belonging (rebuilding infrastructure, landmarks, cultural sites with sentimental value in disaster recovery to restore emotional healing and identity)
Community Engagement and Participation (involving affected communities in recovery decision-making to promote agency, ownership, and collective resilience)
Healing and Mental Health Support (collaborating with mental health professionals to provide counseling, trauma-informed care, support groups in disaster recovery)
Creating Safe and Inclusive Spaces (designing public spaces that promote social interaction, community gathering, activities for psychological healing in disaster recovery)
Long-Term Resilience and Sustainability (incorporating disaster risk reduction, sustainable infrastructure, environmentally friendly practices in rebuilding to instill security and confidence)
Collaboration and Partnerships (fostering partnerships among stakeholders for comprehensive and effective recovery strategies)
transferability_limits: Results can vary according to participant profiles, context, and culture.

Study conducted with a specific age group (20-29, young adults), which may lead to emphasis on certain concepts (e.g., social activities, having fun) over others (e.g., belonging, roots for older people).
Turkish context (collectivist culture) may yield different results compared to individualistic Western societies.
Literature review primarily used Western sources, potentially overlooking Eastern perspectives.
Mood fluctuations and occasion-specific influences can affect individual responses in well-being research.
limitations: The study's reliance on fuzzy cognitive mapping, while robust for complex systems, may be influenced by mood fluctuations and occasion-specific factors, potentially affecting the generalizability of findings.

The focus group participants were a relatively homogeneous group (20-29 years old, from a specific neighborhood in Ankara), which may have led to an emphasis on certain concepts (e.g., social activities, having fun) while underrepresenting others (e.g., belonging, roots, which might be more prominent for older generations or different cultural backgrounds).
The theoretical framework primarily drew from Western literature, potentially limiting the cultural diversity of the concepts explored and their applicability to collectivist cultures like Turkey.
The atmosphere of the study location or recent social events could influence participants' emotional states and responses.

instruments_used.name: Semi-structured interviews
instruments_used.construct: Place attachment, well-being, and related experiences
instruments_used.description: In-depth interviews exploring participants' experiences and perceptions of their attachment to places and its impact on their well-being.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The paper synthesizes existing conceptualizations of place attachment, proposing a multi-faceted model that integrates cognitive, affective, and behavioral dimensions.
The paper integrates different perspectives on well-being (e.g., hedonic, eudaimonic), arguing that place attachment contributes to various forms of well-being.
The paper operates within the framework of environmental psychology, assuming that human-environment interactions are fundamental to psychological well-being and the development of place bonds.

mechanism_chain.description: Social activities foster a sense of community and belonging, which in turn strengthens emotional and cognitive bonds to a place, leading to increased place attachment.
